stem: Some of the writers whose interviews with the Paris Review are included in this volume were caught in the final years of their lives, and these interviews thus lend ____ mood to the collection.

Throughout his career he has never displayed a disinterested respect for the truth—for what was actually said and done rather than for what the wishes bad been. Given such a (i)____ historical fact, it will certainly be seen as (ii)____ that he should now embark on publishing a magazine ostensibly dedicated to history.

Despite the (i)____ nature of contemporary science, the (ii)____ of many individuals (iii)____: the work of women and minority scientists has too often been exploited or deemed rudimentary and unworthy of inclusion into science history books.

In the academic world, the peer-review process and editorial deliberations are largely ____, with only brief traces of these discussions appearing in acknowledgement sections or the occasional footnote that mentions a reviewer’s critique.
Cooper was one of the twentieth century’ s most ____ intellectuals: throughout a very long life he took up a great many causes, most of them unpopular.

While some studies have made claims for dogs’ superiority to cats in terms of intelligence(and other studies have made the opposite claim), it is more widely recognized that, because of the huge differences in these animals’ instinctual priorities, such comparisons are ____.

Throughout human history, intelligence and consciousness have been ____ concepts: those possessing much of the former are assumed, in some ill-defined way, to be more conscious than those less astute.
